_about: Documented municipal water-supply crises (shortage / rationing / quality). Curated by hand; review twice a year. radius_km = area the crisis applies to around lat/lon. severity: severe (chronic, emergency declared, trucked water) or moderate (recurring seasonal rationing).

items.name: Santa Marta
items.summary: Chronic shortfall: public calamity declared over water shortages, the utility (ESSMAR) taken over by Superservicios, water trucks supplying 40+ neighbourhoods, illegal water vendors; the Pozos Colorados desalination plant was cancelled.
sources: Blu Radio — Superservicios toma la empresa de acueducto
El Tiempo — carrotanques a más de 40 barrios

items.name: San Andrés island
items.summary: Island supply is rationed: the Ombudsman reported water reaching households about once every 15 days; public calamity, road blockades and tanker supply in dry seasons.
sources: MinVivienda — calamidad pública en San Andrés

items.name: Alta & Media Guajira (Uribia, Manaure)
items.summary: Most Wayuu rancherías have no piped supply; water comes from jagüeyes, brackish wells and tankers. National government is drilling wells and regional schemes as emergency measures.
sources: MinVivienda — pozo de agua subterránea en Uribia
MinVivienda — esquemas regionales en La Guajira

items.name: Maicao
items.summary: Town supply depends on emergency groundwater wells added by the national government.

items.name: Riohacha
items.summary: Supply from the Tapias river; recurrent low river levels force savings calls and rationing.
sources: El Tiempo — bajos niveles del río Tapias

items.name: Cartagena
items.summary: Acuacar ran weeks of neighbourhood-by-neighbourhood rationing in May–June 2026 (about 50,000 users per round).
sources: RCN — plan de racionamiento en Cartagena
